reason: A bare _: string stays text only under a term outside the "@id"-typed terms. Under type, role and location `decode_jsonld_value` drops it with a warning (see the bare-type row of test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_blank_node_reference_is_dropped_with_a_warning). The bare-attr and prov-type-key rows pin that `decode_jsonld_value` returns the string under ex:attr and under the prov:type key. The null-value row pins that `_decode_value_object` returns the null "@value" as it stands, which the model skips, so no warning follows. Planted faults, whole suite. Inverting the `term not in ID_TYPED_TERMS` test in `decode_jsonld_value` fails the bare-attr and prov-type-key rows. Turning the text of a value object into a string in `_decode_value_object` fails only the null-value row. This test guards over-dropping next to the dropped-with-a-warning test.

`decode_jsonld_value` drops a blank-node reference with one `ProvWarning`, and only that value goes (#609). test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_bare_blank_label_stays_text_and_null_value_warns_nothing guards the opposite over-dropping.

`decode_jsonld_statement` reads a relation "@id" of _:u as anonymous, because a blank node names no record (spec 5, section 3.7). test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_blank_node_reference_is_dropped_with_a_warning covers attribute values, not the statement "@id".

`decode_jsonld_document` rejects a bundle "@id" equal to the "@vocab" IRI. It calls `ProvDocument.add_bundle`, whose `_bundle_identifier` resolves the id with `ProvBundle.mandatory_valid_qname`, and wraps the model error under the label from `_statement_name`.

A caller's object_pairs_hook still sees every pair when `ProvJSONLDSerializer.deserialize` chains `_repeated_key_hook` (#532). It uses the same helper as test_json.py::test_caller_object_pairs_hook_still_sees_every_pair through a different public reader, so it is no duplicate. It lacks the repeated-key half of that PROV-JSON twin.

One dict-valued Entity term is below the majority of the record-type terms that `_is_embedded_submission_context` needs, so `_decode_context` hands the map to `_register_context_namespaces`, which skips the dict value and registers ex. The test pins both steps. Planted faults, whole suite. Counting any one match as the embedded context fails only this test. Removing the dict-value skip in `_register_context_namespaces` fails this test, test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_mixed_context_registers_namespace_prefixes and test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_empty_key_beside_a_null_vocab_declares_the_default. Its lines match those of the mixed test apart from the second context key (Entity here, myTerm there). Keep both. A later audit may send the pair to the verifier as a possible merge with two rows.

@version, "@base" and "@language" keys do not hide the namespace map from `_is_embedded_submission_context` or `_register_context_namespaces`. Ending the loop of `_register_context_namespaces` at the first non-string value fails only this test (planted fault, whole suite). It adds the assertion that the default namespace stays unset, which test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_mixed_context_registers_namespace_prefixes does not make.

`_register_context_namespaces` reads an empty-string key in a context map as the default namespace. test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_empty_key_beside_a_null_vocab_declares_the_default covers the variant with a null "@vocab".

`_register_context_namespaces` raises when an empty-string key and "@vocab" in one context object give different IRIs. test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_empty_key_beside_a_null_vocab_declares_the_default is the neighbouring case where "@vocab" is null.

`_register_context_namespaces` skips a non-string "@vocab" value and still declares the empty-string key as the default namespace. test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_empty_context_key_declares_the_default_namespace covers the plain case.
`_add_memberships` gives every record of an identified Membership with an array the "@id" and the attributes, with no warning (submission section 4.18).

`_add_memberships` keeps the "@id" of an identified Membership with one member. It runs the same code as test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_identified_membership_array_gives_every_member_the_id with a list of length 1.

An IRI under "@id", a bare IRI under type, and a datatype given by name or by IRI each resolve to the qualified name through `ProvBundle.mandatory_valid_qname`. The node-reference row passes through `decode_jsonld_value` and `_decode_node_reference`, the type row through the bare-string path of `decode_jsonld_value`, and the datatype rows through `_decode_value_object`. The node-reference row is the takeover of the removed test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_node_reference_with_absolute_iri and is the only test that reads an absolute-IRI node reference and expects it compacted, so a later narrowing of this test must keep that row.

A document's own rdf binding wins over the submission one, because `_decode_context` checks the scope before it registers the submission binding (#724). test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_resolves_rdf_in_a_bundle covers the bundle scope.

Each malformed document raises `ProvJSONLDException` with its message. The raise comes from `decode_jsonld_document` (the PROV-JSON shape, a "@graph" that is no array, a Bundle with no "@id"), `_expect_object` (a "@graph" entry that is no object), `_decode_statement_type`, or `decode_jsonld_statement` (an element with no "@id", and the wrapper of every error from `_decode_statement_attributes`, `_decode_value_object`, `_decode_formal_time`, `ProvRecord._check_repeated_value` and `ProvBundle.mandatory_valid_qname`). Rows share arcs in groups (the three "@type" rows, the two value-object "@type" rows) but differ in input shape (None, int, list), so they stay. The Mention row is the reader side of C2 on docs/reference/conformance.md. test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_name_no_namespace_resolves_is_rejected covers the names no namespace resolves.
`decode_jsonld_statement` raises for an empty entity array.
`decode_jsonld_statement` and `_add_memberships` turn an entity array into one hadMember record per distinct member (submission section 4.18). The repeated-member row has its own list shape.

`decode_jsonld_statement` raises and names a member no namespace resolves, because it resolves each member with `ProvBundle.mandatory_valid_qname` before `_add_memberships` runs. `_add_memberships` raises nothing itself. Replacing that resolution with the raw member (planted fault) failed no test of the suite, so this test pins the rejection of the member and not that one call. test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_name_no_namespace_resolves_is_rejected covers the other positions, with a row for a member.

A one-element entity array reads as one record through `decode_jsonld_statement` (submission section 4.18, ProvToolbox output). It could be a row of test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_membership_entity_array_gives_one_record_per_member with its own expected value, but the record-count assertion differs, so it stays.

A namespace map that holds a dict-valued term (myTerm, which is no record-type name) still registers its string prefixes, because `_register_context_namespaces` skips only the dict value. Planted faults, whole suite. Removing that skip fails this test, test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_context_with_one_colliding_term_registers_namespace_prefixes and test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_empty_key_beside_a_null_vocab_declares_the_default. Counting any one match as the embedded context in `_is_embedded_submission_context` does not fail it. No planted fault failed this test alone, because the colliding-term test fails under every fault that fails this one. A later audit should send the pair to the verifier as a possible merge with two rows, or as a removal of this test. Its ruling stays keep until then.

A name that no namespace resolves raises the model's sentence under the statement label, in every position (#609, #673, #725). The positions reach `decode_jsonld_statement`, `decode_jsonld_value`, `_decode_statement_attributes` and `ProvBundle.mandatory_valid_qname`, and `_statement_name` builds the label of each. The bundle-id row raises from `decode_jsonld_document`. Rows share arcs in groups (three bare terms, two node references, two datatypes), but each position has its own label and attribute, so they stay. test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_malformed covers other malformed input.

`decode_jsonld_value` reads a node reference as a qualified name through `_decode_node_reference` and `ProvBundle.mandatory_valid_qname` (#545). Every row passes a dict, so the `term not in ID_TYPED_TERMS` branch of `decode_jsonld_value`, which only a bare string reaches, is never reached here, and inverting it (planted fault) fails no row of this test. The key decides the path in `_decode_statement_attributes`, which maps type and value through SPECIAL_TERM_ATTRS and resolves prov:type and ex:ref through `ProvBundle.mandatory_valid_qname`. Removing the SPECIAL_TERM_ATTRS lookup fails only the type and value rows of this test, and returning the node reference unresolved from `decode_jsonld_value` fails all four rows (planted faults, whole suite). test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_iri_value_is_the_qualified_name covers the IRI forms.

It built the payload of the node-reference row of test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_iri_value_is_the_qualified_name (ex:ref holding one {"@id": EX_URI + "thing"}) and asserted the same compacted qualified name, through `_decode_node_reference` and `decode_jsonld_value`. The takeover row gives the code the identical payload, so any fault in any file has the same outcome in both, and the verifier's four planted faults, the arc check and the mutation rerun found nothing only this test caught. #545 lists no absolute-IRI node reference as a separate defect. After the removal the node-reference row of test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_iri_value_is_the_qualified_name is the only test that reads an absolute-IRI node reference and expects it compacted, so do not narrow that row without reading this.

`_decode_node_reference` raises one message from one statement for six inputs, since a node reference is a lone non-empty string "@id" (#545). Folds in test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_node_reference_with_other_keys_raises (rows extra-value, extra-type, extra-language and extra-property) and test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_node_reference_with_bad_id_raises (rows id-not-a-string and id-empty). Each row builds the same literal node as the originals and keeps match="@id", so nothing was lost.

`_decode_statement_attributes` finds no formal term for a prefix:local key such as prov:activity, because formal_by_term is keyed by local part, so it passes the value on as an other attribute. `ProvBundle.new_record` hands those beside the formal ones to the record class, where `ProvRecord.add_attributes` makes prov:activity the formal activity and `ProvRecord._check_repeated_value` keeps one of two equal values (#783). Planted faults, whole suite. Stripping the prov: prefix before the formal lookup in `_decode_statement_attributes` fails both rows and the two prov:activity rows of test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_malformed. Making `_check_repeated_value` always raise fails only the second row here, among the tests of this module. Dropping the other attributes in `ProvBundle.new_record` fails the first row, among many others.

`ProvJSONLDSerializer.deserialize` installs `_repeated_key_hook`, so a repeated key raises with no position (#532). test_json.py::test_caller_object_pairs_hook_still_sees_every_pair covers the PROV-JSON reader, which is a different reader.

`_decode_context` and `_submission_bindings` let rdf, rdfs and provext names resolve when the document references the submission context (#724). Each row resolves in a different place. The rdfs key row resolves in `_decode_statement_attributes`, the rdf datatype row in `_decode_value_object`, and the provext node-reference row in `decode_jsonld_value` through `_decode_node_reference`. test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_without_the_submission_context_leaves_its_prefixes_undeclared is the negative control.

A bundle's own "@context" scope decides whether rdf resolves and to which IRI (#724). `_decode_context` registers the bindings on the bundle and `NamespaceManager._binding_in_scope` looks the prefix up in scope.

The rdf prefix resolves under a context URL, under an embedded context that `_is_embedded_submission_context` recognises, and under a context where another prefix binds the same IRI (#724). `_decode_context` decides each case.
`_decode_value_object` raises for a value object that has no "@value".

Without the submission context, rdf stays undeclared and `decode_jsonld_value` raises (#724). It guards `_decode_context` against over-registering the submission prefixes, and it sits beside the rejecting rule of test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_name_no_namespace_resolves_is_rejected.
`decode_jsonld_value` keeps a bare string under an extension key as text (#545). test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_bare_blank_label_stays_text_and_null_value_warns_nothing covers the blank-label case.

`decode_jsonld_value` reads a node reference from the ProvToolbox fixture provtoolbox-node-reference.jsonld as a qualified name (#545). test_jsonld.py::test_deserialize_node_reference_under_any_key covers the keys.

`decode_jsonld_value` keeps a string with a colon under an extension key as text (#545). It differs from test_jsonld.py::test_interop_provtoolbox_bare_string_under_extension_key_is_a_string by the colon in the string.

The vendored submission primer decodes through `decode_jsonld_document` to the expected document and round-trips. It is a compatibility fixture. test_jsonld_schema.py::test_interop_fixtures_validate_against_prov_jsonld_schema checks validity only.

`_is_embedded_submission_context` recognises the embedded context whole, and `_decode_context` then registers only its prefixes (#724). test_jsonld.py::test_serialize_context_embed covers the write side.

A qualified-name value survives `ProvJSONLDSerializer.serialize` and `ProvJSONLDSerializer.deserialize` with a prefix or the default namespace, under a URL or an embedded context (#545, #564). The pair `encode_jsonld_value` and `decode_jsonld_value` must agree, and `_decode_context` must register the namespaces. test_jsonld.py::test_serialize_qualified_name_as_node_reference pins only the written shape.

`encode_jsonld_document` writes "@context" plus "@graph", `encode_jsonld_statement` writes bare statement terms, and an anonymous relation carries no "@id" (PROV-JSONLD submission, section 4). test_jsonld_schema.py::test_example_documents_validate_against_prov_jsonld_schema checks validity only, so a change of the written shape that stays schema-valid would go unnoticed without it.

`encode_jsonld_document` writes a bundle as a nested object with its own "@context" and "@graph" (PROV-JSONLD submission). test_jsonld_schema.py::test_example_documents_validate_against_prov_jsonld_schema checks validity only.
`ProvJSONLDSerializer.serialize` raises ValueError for a context option other than "url" or "embed", which is the public option contract.

`ProvJSONLDSerializer.serialize` with context="embed" makes `encode_jsonld_document` put the object that `load_vendored_context` returns into "@context". test_jsonld.py::test_roundtrip_context_embed_registers_only_the_submission_prefixes covers the read side.

`encode_jsonld_document` writes "@vocab" and "@base" with the same IRI for a default namespace, through `_JSONPrefixMap`, so default-namespace "@id" values resolve. test_jsonld_semantics.py::test_expansion_default_namespace_ids_resolve_against_vocab_uri expands the output, while this test pins the exact keys.

A default-namespace attribute called "entity" must not overwrite a Usage's formal "entity", which `encode_jsonld_statement` and `_encode_attribute_term` would otherwise write under one key. The assertion differs from test_jsonld.py::test_serialize_default_namespace_attribute_uses_absolute_iri_key, because the formal value must survive.

`_encode_attribute_term` keys a non-formal attribute of the default namespace by its absolute IRI. A bare local part would look like a term the context defines and fails the schema pattern "prefix:local", and a name such as "type" would collide with a reserved bare term. Folds in test_jsonld.py::test_serialize_default_namespace_attribute_colliding_with_reserved_term as rows plain-local-part and reserved-term, which keep both inputs, both assertions and both comments. Both rows reach the same `not attr.namespace.prefix` clause, because a default-namespace attribute has the prefix "", but they catch different faults. Dropping the prefix check in `_encode_attribute_term` fails only plain-local-part, because RESERVED_BARE_TERMS still catches "type". Looking SPECIAL_ATTR_TERMS up by local part in both the `.get` and the guard of `_encode_attribute_term` fails only reserved-term. Keep both rows. test_jsonld_schema.py::test_default_namespace_attributes_validate_against_prov_jsonld_schema checks validity only and stays.
`encode_jsonld_value` writes a default-namespace name as a bare "@id" that resolves against "@base" (#564). test_jsonld.py::test_roundtrip_qualified_name_value does not pin the written shape.

`encode_jsonld_statement` raises `ProvJSONLDException` for a Mention, because PROV-JSONLD has no Mention term (C2 on docs/reference/conformance.md). It is a permanent, documented limitation and the rubric names it protected.

`encode_jsonld_document` and `_JSONPrefixMap` write neither "@vocab" nor "@base" when the document has no default namespace, so no empty "@base" reaches the context. It is the negative control of test_jsonld.py::test_serialize_default_namespace_as_vocab.

`encode_jsonld_value` writes a qualified name under ex:ref, prov:label or prov:value as {"@id": ...}, so a JSON-LD processor reads an IRI node and not a QName literal (#564). test_jsonld_schema.py::test_qualified_name_under_extension_key_validates_against_prov_jsonld_schema checks validity only, not the exact shape.

`encode_jsonld_value` keeps a qualified name under type, location or role as a bare string, because the submission context types those terms as "@id" (#564). test_jsonld.py::test_serialize_qualified_name_as_node_reference covers the other terms. The role row builds a Usage, an input shape the other rows lack.

`encode_jsonld_statement` and `encode_jsonld_value` write a prov:type value as a bare qualified name, prov:label as a value object and extra attributes as typed value objects (PROV-JSONLD submission, section 4). test_jsonld_schema.py::test_example_documents_validate_against_prov_jsonld_schema checks validity only and not these exact shapes.
